newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mahathir reverses stand on Malaysian potential.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir reverses stand on Malaysian potential.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said he has reversed a stand made in a book he wrote nearly three decades ago which criticised the seeming inability of Malays to succeed, newspapers reported on Monday.
He said he could now see that Malays had the ability and confidence to do well, The Star newspaper reported.

"I admit that at the time I felt very disappointed. I spoke to many people my age then who did not have the confidence. I too was not confident that Malays could achieve success," he was quoted as saying on Sunday.

"Now I reverse my stand. I no longer believe what I had written in The Malay Dilemma," he said at a forum celebrating the 51st anniversary of his dominant political party, United Malays National Organisation.
The Malay Dilemma, first published in 1970, was written when mahathir was a young physician. It was banned by the government soon after its publication.
The ban was lifted when Mahathir became premier in 1981 and has since become a local bestseller.
The Southeast Asian nation is expected to record its 10th straight year of eight percent growth or better this year and has set a programme to become a fully industrialised nation by 2020.
